settings.name: provider
settings.skip: model-router skipped, provider not valid: run setup
settings.notValid: provider: {stored} (not valid: use one of typesafe)
settings.refused: provider unchanged: only a local session can change it

command.name: model-router-provider
command.description: Shows or changes whose model scores subagent calls: typesafe.

settings.name: gateway
settings.skip: model-router skipped, gateway not valid: run setup
settings.notValid: gateway: {stored} (not valid: use one of direct, auto, openrouter-first, openrouter)
settings.useOneOf: gateway: use one of direct, auto, openrouter-first, openrouter
settings.refused: gateway unchanged: only a local session can change it

command.name: model-router-gateway
command.description: Shows or changes how OpenRouter is used for the provider: direct, auto, openrouter-first, openrouter.

description.description: One line that says what this task is. model-router sends it with the goal to Jev, which judges the model and effort the child needs.

reasoning_effort.description: Leave it unset unless you re-dispatch a failed task. The child runs at this effort, and model-router still picks its model. A delegation.reasoning_effort in the user's config wins.

level.description: Leave it unset unless you re-dispatch a failed task. 0 runs the child on the user's small model, 1 on the user's middle model, 2 on the large model, and model-router asks Jev nothing. A level whose model is not set runs on the model Hermes gives it. A routed task's label shows its level as L0, L1 or L2. A model in the user's delegation config wins.

delegationAddendum: model-router picks each task's model and effort. Give every task a description. Leave reasoning_effort and level unset unless you re-dispatch a failed task; the model-router-hermes:model-router skill says how.

texts.toolDescription: Reads the router's settings. It returns the provider, the gateway, the three models, and whether each key the settings allow is set. It changes nothing and never returns a key.
